answer: Fake identities arrive as a crowd vouching for itself. The fix is a trust graph where weight comes not from the count of endorsers but from how many independent clusters they span, measured by funding and timing. A newcomer starts as a flat mesa, rising only when unrelated groups attest. Colluding accounts from one source collapse into one cluster and count once. Endorsements carry liability: if a protégé proves fraudulent, the endorser loses standing, so vouching is costly. An ivory record of who backed whom persists, and a relic of past collusion stays visible after those accounts retire.
